notes.grade: A tutorial map never streamed beside another, so it may take its own grade. Saturation 1.1 over SATURATION_FORWARD (0.69 to 0.76) gives back some of the chroma the shared grade takes from its props, sea and court; the court keeps its own colour (`ground`).
notes.ground: Its courts and yards are Walk_ decks from wall to wall, which LookGround paints as roads unless the region says otherwise: path_tint x path_luma x the texture's grain, dropping each deck's own colour. At the defaults every tutorial court came out one road beige (echo_court, wayfarer_bastion, lantern_exchange and waystone_yard drew identical frames). The migration worked round it with a path tint matched to develop's court (path_tint [1.0, 0.979, 0.496], path_luma_forward 0.301), which could give the map only one colour and dropped the flagstones' own tone variation (court world std 21 against develop's 30). deck_path 0 (integration) paints its decks as its own ground: each keeps its own colour with the yard lift, whatever its hue, and none is edged like a road. Its two decks (the flagstone court and the packed road) keep their own colours, cream and orange. deck_tint multiplies each deck's own linear colour: the grade warms and greys a kept court (Reedway's meadow came out olive-brown, Bellwatch's cream grey), so it was solved from develop's court colour over three Forward+ renders (integration runs int_small_2 to int_small_4, ground box in boxes_small_maps). Court now (188, 184, 147) luminance 182 against develop's (213, 210, 158) 207. Develop's court is blown out there, so the court is aimed at luminance 185, where the migration's tint put it. Forward+ only in effect: the compatibility renderer was not measured and keeps the tint too.
